mechanism: Count the T-tetrominoes by stem direction. Ts with the stem on the canonical up side (stem at row-1) produce palette[3] marks at corners (0,0),(2,0),(0,2),(2,2) of a 3x6 canvas, in that order. Ts with the stem on the down side produce palette[1] marks at the same corners +3 columns. Background is palette[0] and objects are palette[2]. The factory maps the up vector (-1,0), the bar vector (0,1) and all 8 tally cells forward through the transformed() D4 convention: column reversal when d4>=4, then (d4%4) clockwise turns. The emitted solve() runs on visible coordinates. It counts a stem cell s for direction d when s-d and its two bar neighbours are FG, the two bar-axis neighbours of s are not FG, and s+d is not FG. This handles bars that touch or share a cell on the same border row, which native allows because its adjacency check only looks at interior cells. There is no first/majority fallback, no D4 search, no demo skipping and no label use.
constructor_defect: The random branch samples (row,col,cdir) with replacement. An exact duplicate paints the same cells and its ids overwrite its twin, so the interior adjacency check passes. cdirs.count() still tallies it, so the label counts an object that is invisible in the input. Two identical-input/different-label witnesses are in d5c634a2-evidence-report.json native_witnesses, both produced by native generate() with legal random-branch latents. No visible-coordinate program can match the native labels on these inputs.
proposed_fix: proposed_constructor.py (see proposed_constructor.diff): in the random branch, reject a draw if len(set(zip(rows, cols, cdirs))) < len(cdirs). Nothing else changes. Size range, num_boxes, count bounds, border-row merges (235/4000 proposed pairs keep merged border bars) and the explicit validate() fixture path are all preserved, so the canonical fixtures are byte-identical.
